Class ScanUrl

java.lang.Object
de.hallerweb.enterprise.prioritize.ui.common.ScanUrl
public final class ScanUrl extends Object
Builds the absolute URL that goes onto a physical NFC sticker, pointing at the scan page.

Why the address comes from the request. The application does not know — and deliberately does not configure — the address it is reachable under; the scan page itself only ever emits relative links. But a sticker needs an absolute URL, and there is one address that is known to work: the one the admin's browser is talking to right now. It loaded this GUI from it, so it resolves and it is reachable. Reading it off the incoming request means an admin who opens the GUI as http://192.168.178.10:8080 gets exactly that host on the sticker, with no setting to keep in sync.

The corollary is the warning looksLocalOnly(String) exists for: an admin working on the server itself sees localhost, and a phone tapping a sticker written with that name would resolve it to the phone. A sticker is only as good as the address baked into it.

Author:
peter haller

  • Method Details

    • origin

      public static String origin(jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletRequest request)
      The scheme/host/port the given request was addressed with, as an origin without a trailing slash (e.g. http://192.168.178.10:8080). The default port of the scheme is omitted, so an installation behind 80/443 yields the short form a person would write down.

    • forTag

      public static String forTag(String origin, String uuid)
      The URL to store on the tag with the given uuid, as an NDEF URL record.
      Parameters:
      origin - scheme/host/port, as returned by origin(HttpServletRequest)
      uuid - the uuid the NfcUnit was registered with

    • looksLocalOnly

      public static boolean looksLocalOnly(String origin)
      Whether the origin names the machine the browser itself runs on. Such an address is fine for clicking around the GUI and useless on a sticker — the phone would resolve it to itself — so the panel showing these URLs warns instead of pretending they are ready to write.
